text:
The bones of the middle finger, in order from the hand outward, are the third metacarpal (in the palm), then the proximal phalanx, the middle phalanx, and the distal phalanx at the fingertip. The middle finger has no separate carpal bones, since those belong to the wrist. Its sesamoids, which are small bones that can sit in the flexor tendons, are not part of the standard sequence.

CONFIDENCE: 97
